name: Isolated Digestive Duplication Cyst of the Tongue

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Lingual Digestive Duplication Cyst

criteria.description: Presence of a cystic lesion localized within the tongue tissue
Histological confirmation of a cyst lined by gastrointestinal-type epithelium
Imaging (MRI/CT/Ultrasound) showing a well-defined cystic mass without communication to the oral cavity or digestive tract
No evidence of digestive tract duplications elsewhere

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (anatomical location, histopathology, and imaging characteristics) must be met for diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathological examination is essential to differentiate from other cystic lesions of the tongue.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lingual cystic mass with gastrointestinal epithelial lining
searchTerms: cystic tongue mass with digestive tissue
fluid-filled tongue lump with GI lining

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital midline or lateral tongue swelling
pathognomonic.notes: Typically present at birth or early infancy
searchTerms: midline or side tongue lump present at birth

common.symptomName: Dysphagia due to tongue mass effect
searchTerms: swallowing problems due to tongue swelling

common.notes: Impaired tongue mobility or mass interference

common.symptomName: Oral discomfort or foreign body sensation
common.notes: Patient reports sensation of fullness or irritation
searchTerms: feeling of something stuck in mouth

common.notes: Visible or palpable mass on tongue examination

occasional.notes: May occur due to trauma or infection

occasional.symptomName: Infection of the cyst leading to cellulitis

occasional.notes: Rare but possible in large cysts obstructing airway
searchTerms: respiratory distress due to oral swelling

occasional.notes: Due to cyst proximity to salivary ducts

rare.notes: Extremely rare, reported in isolated cases
Rare involvement of lingual nerve causing paresthesia
searchTerms: nerve pain or weakness from compression
neurological symptoms due to mass effect

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests unless secondary infection present
Inflammatory markers elevated if cyst infected
imaging: MRI: well-circumscribed cystic lesion within tongue musculature
Ultrasound: anechoic or hypoechoic cystic mass without vascular flow
CT scan: cystic lesion with fluid density, no communication with oral cavity
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Histopathology: cyst lined by gastrointestinal-type epithelium with smooth muscle layer
No communication with digestive tract confirmed surgically or radiologically

distinguishingFeatures: Thyroglossal duct cyst typically midline and moves with swallowing or tongue protrusion
Ranula is a mucous retention cyst arising from sublingual gland
Usually located in floor of mouth rather than tongue
Lined by squamous or respiratory epithelium, not gastrointestinal
Contains ectodermal elements such as hair follicles or sebaceous glands
Histology differs from digestive duplication cyst

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of tongue mass
Signs of cyst infection or abscess formation
references: Friedrich RE. Lingual duplication cysts: a review of the literature and report of a case. Head Face Med. 2010;6:17.
